transcript:
Header: 2027-08-10 14:30 UTC | Duration: 48 minutes | Attendees: Maya, Diego, Priya (Redwood) + Alicia, Tom, Nina, Samir (Southstrand)

Summary: quick intro and objectives then deep into VPC and pilot logistics. Some transcription noise - names and acronyms may be fuzzy.

00:00 - Maya Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, uh, this is Maya from Redwood, I'm the AE on the account. Appreciate you carving out time. Um, quick round robin - who do we have from Southstrand?
00:12 - Alicia Reed: Alicia here, CTO. Thanks Maya.
00:15 - Tom Hargreaves: Tom, Platform Eng.
00:18 - Nina Okafor: Nina, Security.
00:20 - Samir Patel: Samir, data science.
00:22 - Maya Chen: Great — Priya our CSM and Diego our SE are on as well. Goal today: align pilot success metrics, confirm network and security needs, and handoff runbook so we can start the sandbox next week.
00:40 - Priya Patel: Hi team, short note: our onboarding runbook has a few checkpoints — access, VPC, test data, and eval prompts. We'll use those to gate the pilot go/no-go.
00:54 - Tom Hargreaves: Sounds good. On data — we have a sample anonymized set for Samir to share, but we also have a couple of internal latency-sensitive flows. We're worried about p99 spikes.
01:10 - Diego Ramos: Right — p99 is where batching and KV cache behavior matters. For the pilot we can run two configurations: 1) Redwood Private in your VPC with reserved GPUs; 2) Hosted Redwood for fast iteration. Private gives control over egress and KMS, hosted is faster to stand up.
01:35 - Alicia Reed: Our security team prefers VPC. We also have strict key rotation policies and we want HSM-backed KMS. Do you support external KMS or BYOK?
01:50 - Diego Ramos: Yes, we support external KMS integrations and HSM-based keys — there's a config for Bring Your Own Key for Private deployments. There are a few operational notes though: key rotation timing can affect long-lived sessions if not coordinated with token refresh.
02:10 - Nina Okafor: Hmm, token refresh being disrupted could break inference caches? We need to understand operational blast radius.
02:20 - Diego Ramos: Correct — if you rotate keys mid-session the connection to the model runtime needs the new key for decrypting the model artifacts, but runtime will gracefully fallback when configured. We'll send a doc with recommended rotation windows.
02:40 - Priya Patel: I'll add that to the runbook notes.
02:45 - Tom Hargreaves: On networking — we run in us-east-1 primarily. We'll share CIDR ranges but want to limit open egress. Is there an IP allowlist approach?
02:58 - Diego Ramos: Yep, we can do VPC peering or PrivateLink. For strict egress control we recommend VPC peering + endpoint, and we can provide the expected IP ranges for the pilot. For dedicated pools there are fixed node IP ranges per AZ.
03:20 - Samir Patel: For the pilot success metrics: we care about inference latency under load, cost per 1k tokens, and correctness on our prompt suite. We'll provide 10 representative prompts.
03:38 - Maya Chen: Perfect — that's aligned with our typical pilot KPI set. For correctness we can run evals in Redwood Optimize and hook regression alerts to the prompt set.
03:50 - Alicia Reed: What about model versions? We need version pinning for audit.
03:55 - Diego Ramos: You can pin a model version and we support canary rollouts — can route a small percentage to a new version and have automatic fallback. The console shows token-level cost and latency per route.
04:15 - Nina Okafor: Audit logs — will actions be logged at token-level with request IDs? We need that for investigations.
04:25 - Priya Patel: Yes, audit logs capture request IDs, model, route, user token id — we also have retention settings as an add-on if you need longer retention.
04:35 - Alicia Reed: Transmission and rest at rest encryption on by default?
04:40 - Diego Ramos: All traffic is TLS, and at rest encryption uses CMK — for Private you can attach your CMK.
04:50 - Tom Hargreaves: Ok. On sizing: the workload has a heavy tail, some requests 4k tokens. Are there recommendations for batch size and quantization?
05:05 - Diego Ramos: We typically recommend dynamic batching with small max batch size for latency-sensitive calls and larger batch for background bulk. For 4k sequences, we choose kernels optimized for long seqs — quantization tradeoffs depend on model family. We'll run two quantization profiles in the pilot and measure quality/regression.
05:30 - Samir Patel: Will that change the model outputs? We can't accept a >2% drop in rouge/accuracy on our tests.
05:40 - Maya Chen: We'll capture that in the success criteria. Diego, can you own the evaluation config to ensure we meet the 2% guardrail?
05:48 - Diego Ramos: Yep, I'll set up the eval harness and share the baseline.
06:00 - Priya Patel: Timing: customer wants a two-week pilot then a go/no-go. Proposed timeline: Week 1 - networking & smoke tests; Week 2 - load test & evals.
06:15 - Alicia Reed: That works for us. We need to sync on on-call contacts during Week 1.
06:22 - Priya Patel: I'll add an on-call rotation to the runbook, plus a 1-hour daily stand for Week 1.
06:30 - Tom Hargreaves: On cost — what's the expected monthly burn if we go dedicated after pilot? Ballpark for 4 GPUS?
06:40 - Maya Chen: Ballpark depends on commitment and utilization. Diego, can you provide two scenarios — baseline reserved (70% utilization) and burst (30% on-demand)?
06:50 - Diego Ramos: Yes, I'll run a quick model with current list price and show unit token cost at the different utilization tiers.
07:00 - Samir Patel: For the pilot we'll need an S3 connector to pull test artifacts. Any special networking for that?
07:08 - Diego Ramos: That's fine — for Private deployments we usually create a VPC endpoint to S3 or allow specific IAM roles. We'll include that in the VPC checklist.
07:20 - Nina Okafor: Security Q: SAML integration — can we map assertions to internal user groups and enforce RBAC?
07:30 - Priya Patel: Yes, Redwood supports SAML with group mapping for role-based access and we can provision RBAC roles in the console. We'll need a SAML metadata file from you.
07:42 - Alicia Reed: We'll send the metadata. Also, do you provide data residency guarantees? We need EU-only for certain flows.
07:52 - Diego Ramos: We support region pinning — you can constrain routes to EU regions for data residency. For Private, you can place runtime in a specific region/AZ.
08:05 - Tom Hargreaves: Ok great. Anything else on the security checklist?
08:10 - Nina Okafor: I'd like to see the incident response playbook and the last penetration test summary — do you share that?
08:18 - Maya Chen: We do. We'll share a redacted pentest exec summary and IR playbook after we exchange NDAs if needed. Priya will coordinate.
08:30 - Priya Patel: Noted — I'll include that in the doc bundle.
08:35 - Maya Chen: Quick demo idea — if we spin up a hosted endpoint earlier tonight we could run a few sample prompts to surface any immediate mismatch. Is the team comfortable with a short smoke test on hosted?
08:48 - Alicia Reed: Yeah, we can do a hosted smoke test for functional checks, but pilot will be Private.
09:00 - Tom Hargreaves: Who's ownership for the runbook tasks?
09:05 - Priya Patel: I'll be the runbook owner for coordination. Diego owns technical setup. Maya will follow on commercial and exec updates.
09:15 - Maya Chen: Great. Let's recap next steps. Diego to send cost/latency estimate and VPC IP ranges. Priya to send onboarding runbook, Slack invite, and doc bundle. Southstrand to send sample prompts, dataset link, and SAML metadata. We'll plan a sizing call the week of Aug 23.
09:40 - Alicia Reed: Perfect. One small ask — can you include a short checklist for canary rollback in case a model update regresses?
09:48 - Diego Ramos: Yes — rollback steps + how to flip traffic in the console.
09:55 - Maya Chen: Thanks everyone. We'll follow up over email and put the artifacts in the shared folder.
10:05 - Meeting ends.

Notes about transcript quality: speaker overlaps occasionally, some proper nouns may be spelled phonetically.
